cands.bio: Republican member of the Alabama Senate for District 32 (Baldwin County) since November 2018. Former chairman of the Baldwin County Commission and small business owner. Earlier worked in emergency management for the Commonwealth of Virginia and for Virginia Power.
cands.gaps: We found no documented action or stated position from Elliott on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, immigration enforcement or H-1B, gun laws, abortion, or school vouchers. His campaign site lists bills he sponsored, such as an arrest-without-warrant bill for parole violators and a housing tax credit, but we could not confirm them from legislative records, so we left them out. We could not find when he served as Baldwin County Commission chairman, or when he returned to Baldwin County after working in Virginia. No endorsements were listed for the 2026 race. No news reporting on controversies was in the pages we had. Ballotpedia says he did not complete its candidate survey.

local.label: Roots 100: Wikipedia says he was born and raised in Mobile and Baldwin counties, and his campaign site says the same. He left for college and work in Virginia, then returned to Baldwin County to raise his family. · Money: 2% of money from District 32 ZIP codes after leaving out land and development money (3% before)

qual.background: State senator since 2018, with seats on the Finance and Taxation General Fund and Judiciary committees. cands.bio: Janet Appleby was the Democratic nominee for Alabama State Senate District 32 in 2026. She advanced without a primary contest and lost the general election to incumbent Republican Chris Elliott. The sources give no other biographical details.

endorsements.text: Listed by Ballotpedia as receiving voter guide recommendations from Tabitha's List: Candidates You Can Trust (a Sway voting group run by Tabitha Isner) and Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy (a Sway voting group run by Tevin (Momala) Davis).

cands.gaps: We could not find where Janet Appleby was born or raised, when she came to Alabama, or her work history. We found no record of any public office she has held. She did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey, and we found no campaign website, interviews or questionnaires with her stated positions. We found no documented stances on data centers or development, no controversies, and no foreign ties. We also found no record of any actions she took that bear on the issues in this guide.

score.why: Raised $4,712, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
